_comment: Test pipeline baselines. Update deliberately when counts legitimately change. wrapper_stripped_count is the block count the generator's SwiftWrapperPostProcessor.Process removes from the wrapper; the harness reuses that oracle. The count is 0. Internal-type and Swift-unavailable references are not strip candidates: they remain for compiler attribution and verify/recover withdrawal. Only deterministic placeholder cleanup can increment this count, and any increase fails the gate. Reseed with `nuke seed-wrapper-strip-baseline`.
_coverage_comment: Coverage ratchet budgets enforced by build/scripts/coverage-report.py (compare_coverage_baseline). Each count is the accepted ceiling; the gate fails on any INCREASE and reports decreases as improvements to tighten. must_pass_degraded = must-pass features whose binding compiles but skips ≥1 member; must_pass_compiled_out = must-pass features whose binding member(s) were compiled out for this SDK; must_pass_passing_untested = must-pass features that bind cleanly but have no runtime test referencing them in RuntimeTestsApp; known_unsupported_total = declared known-unsupported features. Seeded from a fresh compile-only run under the CI Xcode. generator_exit_code was removed: it duplicated the regen-exit gate (a non-zero generator exit already hard-fails --compile-only) and nothing read it. must_pass_degraded moved 1->26 when conformance losses stopped being silent: a conformance to a protocol with no type record now reports a row instead of vanishing, so features that had always lost those conformances began carrying skip rows. 70 of the 74 rows are ConformanceProtocolNotInTypeDatabase against stdlib/Foundation marker protocols (BitwiseCopyable, RawRepresentable, CVarArg, _KeyValueCodingAndObserving) that have no type record and were never bindable; 25 of the 26 features carry conformance-reason rows exclusively. convention_c holds the only member-level skips and is the feature the previous ceiling of 1 described. Nothing left the emitted surface in the same window — the api-manifest gate fails on a removed member and stayed green, and the skip-surface gate found one new marker corpus-wide, not 25 features' worth. must_pass_passing_untested tightened 33->31 as two features moved into that same reporting shift. must_pass_degraded counts LOST surface only: rows whose reason the generator classifies as declared-but-degraded (published in binding-report.json as SkipTriage.DeclaredButDegradedReasons) name a member that IS emitted and are reported as a separate callout rather than ratcheted, so naming a previously-anonymous degrade cannot move this ceiling. must_pass_degraded moved 26->27 and must_pass_passing_untested tightened 31->28 when skip attribution began resolving a nested type to its outermost declaration: a member of Outer.Inner was charged by its innermost short name, so a nested type borrowed the source file of any unrelated top-level namesake (a nested Token's generic-constructor skip degraded the three top-level class features) or matched no owned declaration and vanished. The one added degraded feature is nested_struct, whose NestedOuter.Inner carries a BitwiseCopyable ConformanceProtocolNotInTypeDatabase row that was previously dropped that way.
